rules.rule: ne = I, nang = you, alang = he/she. Plural = + -tum (netum 'we, excluding you'; etum ~ itum 'we, including you'; alang-tum 'they'). Honorific = + -li before -tum (nang-li, ne-li).

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.notes: English 'you' needs a casual/polite choice; English 'we' needs an including-you/excluding-you choice. The app must ask.

rules.rule: Possession: K gives prefixes ne- (my), nang- (your), a- (his/her): nephi 'my grandmother', nangpo 'your father'. J writes the possessor and noun as separate words (ne hem 'my house', nang hem, la a-hem 'his house') with a- on the second noun in some cases.

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

sources.loc: p.78 Genitive: ne hem, nang hem, la a-hem

rules.notes: Kin terms are probably prefixed (K); other nouns may be separate words (J). Speaker to confirm per noun class.

rules.rule: Predominantly SOV. Time adverbs and free postpositions may come before or after the subject (pini ne bajar dampo; dakchi ne do; la atumi vaylo). Subject is optional in commands.

sources.example: pini ne bajar dampo ~ damji = "I will/shall go to the market today"

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)
sources.loc: constituent order section: verb-final, flexible order of arguments

rules.notes: Template order may be TIME SUBJ DEST VERB or SUBJ TIME DEST VERB. Both are documented.

rules.rule: Inanimate place goals are unmarked with 'go': ne hem damlo 'I went home'; pini ne bajar dampo. Human/animate goals take an allative marker. K describes -long (a-long) as a locative/allative relator.

sources.loc: p.79 Allative: only human and animate nouns are marked

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.notes: Template 1 uses an unmarked place word (documented by J). Speaker to confirm for 'school'.

rules.rule: Day words such as pini 'today' are unmarked. Clock time takes the locative -chi (baji kethomchi 'at three o'clock').

sources.loc: p.79 Locative; p.147 baji kethomchi neli hem damji

rules.rule: pini = today, penap = tomorrow, (a)tumi = yesterday, non = now.

rules.notes: Spelling varies: tumi / timi / atumi.

rules.rule: Karbi has no tense. Time comes from adverbs plus aspect/mood endings. The bare verb with a time adverb is normal (pini la iskul dun = 'he goes to school today').

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.notes: Do not label -lo as 'past' in the app.

rules.rule: -lo (realis): J says the action began before speech time and continues (ne an colo 'I eat rice') and may be added optionally when a time adverb is present. K treats it as realis/completed. Neighbor often glosses it as past.

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.notes: English past tense is not a safe mapping for -lo.

rules.rule: -po = definite future; -ji = dubitative / intended future. 'I will come tomorrow' = ne penap vaypo (definite), ne penap vayji (intended). K: -po irrealis 1, -ji irrealis 2.

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.notes: First-person inclusive subjects take -nang (distant) or -lonang (near) future (J p.115).

rules.rule: -bom (continuative) directly after the verb base: ne vaybomlo 'I was coming', ne vaybomlang 'I am still coming', ne vaybompo 'I will be coming'. K also documents -lang 'still'.

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.notes: OCR note: J prints the final nasal as 'y' in this scan; read as -lang.

rules.rule: Perfective -det after the verb; the tense/mood marker follows: damdet 'have gone', damdetlo 'had gone', damdetpo 'will have gone'.

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.rule: Verb negation = repeat the first consonant (cluster) of a monosyllabic root, or of the LAST syllable of a longer root, then -e: klem-kle, vay-ve, dam-de, thek-the. If that syllable begins with a vowel, -e alone. The tense/mood marker follows the negative. With a time adverb the marker may be dropped: ne pini vayve = 'I will not come today'; alayliloy ne damde = 'I will not go with him'.

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.notes: Negated progressive: ne non cobombelang 'I am not eating now' (J p.119): -bom takes the negative (bom -> be).

rules.rule: J writes negation directly before the future marker (latum vayvepo 'they will not come'). K says the negative can combine with irrealis only if perfective -det intervenes (e.g. NEG-PFV-IRR).

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.notes: Dialect or analysis difference. Speaker must choose between dam-de-po and dam-de-det-po (or the bare dam-de).

rules.rule: do = be/exist/have; ave = its negative (hadak ok ave 'there is no fish'; ne hem ave 'I have no house'). kali = 'is not' after nouns/adjectives (la ne mudey kali 'this is not my umbrella').

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.rule: Command endings: -non (also -noi in family speech), -tha (polite, outside family), -tu (command). Prohibitive -ri, optionally + -non: vayri 'don't come', vayrinon. Honorific marker -ik comes before the imperative. The subject is optional.

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.notes: J and K disagree on how -tha is used (J: polite; K: conative). Speaker to confirm each ending.

rules.rule: Let's ___ = verb + -nang (K: hortative). J lists -nang/-lonang for the first-person inclusive future.

sources.doc: Konnerth 2014 (A Grammar of Karbi, Hills Karbi)

rules.notes: Use with the inclusive pronoun etum/itum.

rules.rule: nang + -ji after the verb = must / need to (nang-ji); negated nang-ne = need not.

rules.rule: Yes/no questions take the particle ma after the clause. Question words: kopi what, komat who, konat where.

rules.rule: go = dam (dampo, damji, damlo, damde). J also writes 'pini la iskul dun' for 'he goes to school today'; in K, dun means 'join/together with'.

rules.rule: Respect forms add -li: ne/neli (I), nang/nangli (you), alang/alangli (he/she); plural they = latum (casual) / alanglitum (respectful). Casual forms are used with friends, -li forms when speaking with elders. The choice is about the conversation, not only the person referred to.

sources.example: neli = I when speaking with elders

rules.notes: Matches the -li honorific in Konnerth and Jeyapaul.

rules.rule: '(subject) am/is/are not going' = pronoun + damde for every person; now and habit are both damde; with the word non = now: 'non neli skul damde'. Future: damde lo (to confirm).
rules.notes: Same negative form dam-de predicted by both grammars.

rules.rule: Preferred: Subject - Time - Place - Verb (ne pini skul damde). Also written: Time - Subject - Place - Verb (pini neli skul damde) and Subject - Place - Verb - Time (alangli skul damde pini). The subject must be said. No small word follows the place or 'today'.
rules.notes: Karbi has no word for 'to' (E2).
